equation_request.abstract: We present several families of graphs that allow both efficient quantum walk implementations and efficient quantum walk based search algorithms. For these graphs, we construct quantum circuits that explicitly implement the full quantum walk search algorithm, without reference to a ‘black box’ oracle. These circuits provide a practically implementable method to explore quantum walk based search algorithms with the aim of eventual real-world applications. We also provide a numerical analysis of a quantum walk based search along a twisted toroid family of graphs, which requires O($\sqrt{n}$ log($n$)) elementary 2-qubit quantum gate operations to find a marked node.

specification.problem: Quantum-walk-based spatial search on structured graph families (including a twisted toroid family) implemented as explicit quantum circuits in which the marked node is encoded directly in the circuit rather than through a black-box oracle; the abstract reports O(sqrt(n) log n) elementary 2-qubit gates to find a marked node on the twisted toroid family.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One smallest useful construction chosen as an assumption (no experiment_scope was supplied): a discrete-time coined quantum walk search on a single tiny 4-regular circulant graph taken as a stand-in for a member of the twisted toroid family, with n = 8 vertices (3 position qubits), degree d = 4 (2 coin qubits), one marked vertex w = 0, a Grover coin on unmarked vertices and a -I coin on the marked vertex, a modular-shift operator built from controlled modular increment/decrement circuits, t walk steps, and a final measurement of the position register. Outside scope: the exact definition of the paper's twisted toroid family and the other graph families, the paper's specific circuit decompositions and gate counts, its numerical analysis, and any choice of t or coin that the paper actually used.

equations.label: Circulant stand-in for a twisted toroid instance
equations.latex: V=\mathbb{Z}_n,\quad E=\{\{x,\,x\pm 1 \bmod n\},\ \{x,\,x\pm m \bmod n\} : x\in\mathbb{Z}_n\},\quad n=8,\ m=3
equations.description: A 4-regular circulant graph on n vertices with nearest-neighbour and offset-m connections, used as a tiny concrete instance; all arithmetic on vertex labels is modular reduction mod n.
equations.justification: The abstract names a twisted toroid family but does not define it; a circulant graph with two offsets is a plausible minimal degree-4 graph with a torus-like twisted wrap-around whose shift is implementable by modular adders, but this specific definition is a choice, not paper evidence.
assumptions: The paper's twisted toroid family may be defined differently; this instance is a stand-in only.
n is a power of 2 so that vertex labels fill the position register exactly.

equations.label: Initial state (uniform superposition over coin and position)
equations.description: Equal superposition over all directions and vertices; with d and n powers of 2 this is H^{\otimes 5} applied to |0\rangle^{\otimes 5} on the coin and position registers.
equations.justification: Standard starting state for coined quantum-walk search algorithms (e.g. SKW/AKR-type); the abstract does not state the initial state.
assumptions: Register ordering is coin register then position register, |c\rangle\otimes|x\rangle.

equations.label: Modular shift operator
equations.description: Coin-controlled modular increment/decrement of the position register; implementable as four coin-controlled adders modulo n (each O(log n) elementary gates up to multi-controlled gate decomposition). Equality is exact; addition is reduced mod n.
equations.abstract_quote: allow both efficient quantum walk implementations
equations.justification: An efficient walk implementation on a circulant/toroidal graph is naturally realised by coin-controlled modular adders; this is an inference from the efficiency claim, and the specific 'moving' (coin-preserving) shift convention is a choice.
assumptions: Moving shift (coin unchanged) rather than flip-flop shift.
Position x is encoded in binary on the position register.

equations.label: Marked-vertex-dependent coin (oracle-free marking)
equations.latex: C=C_0\otimes(I_n-|w\rangle\langle w|)+C_1\otimes|w\rangle\langle w|,\quad C_0=2|s\rangle\langle s|-I_d,\ |s\rangle=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt d}\sum_c|c\rangle,\quad C_1=-I_d
equations.description: Grover diffusion coin on unmarked vertices and a sign-flip coin on the marked vertex. Because w is a fixed classical integer, C_1 is applied via a position-controlled operation (X gates mapping |w\rangle to |1\cdots1\rangle, a multi-controlled Z, and the inverse X gates), so no black-box oracle is needed.
equations.abstract_quote: explicitly implement the full quantum walk search algorithm, without reference to a ‘black box’ oracle
equations.justification: The abstract states the marking is implemented explicitly without an oracle; a position-controlled coin conditioned on the classical value w is the standard way to do so. The particular coin choices (Grover coin, -I) are standard SKW-type assumptions, not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: Coin choices C_0 = Grover coin and C_1 = -I are assumed; the paper may use other coins.

equations.label: One step of the walk search and the final state
equations.description: Each step applies the marked-dependent coin then the shift; t steps are applied before measurement.
equations.justification: Standard discrete-time coined quantum-walk search iteration; the abstract does not specify the operator ordering or t.
assumptions: Coin applied before shift within each step.

equations.label: Marked-vertex success probability and gate-count scaling
equations.description: Probability of observing the marked vertex when the position register is measured; the abstract's total gate count is consistent with O(sqrt(n)) steps each costing O(log n) elementary gates (this split is an inference). The optimal t for the tiny instance is not known from the abstract and would need to be scanned numerically.
equations.abstract_quote: requires O($\sqrt{n}$ log($n$)) elementary 2-qubit quantum gate operations to find a marked node
equations.justification: The total O(sqrt(n) log n) gate count is stated in the abstract; the success-probability definition is standard and the decomposition into O(sqrt(n)) steps times O(log n) gates per step is inferred rather than stated.
assumptions: The scaling applies to the paper's twisted toroid family; it is not verified for the stand-in instance.
Asymptotic statement only; constants and the exact t are unknown.

registers.name: coin
registers.role: Encodes the direction c in {0,1,2,3} (d = 4); first register in the tensor product |c>|x>.

registers.name: position
registers.role: Encodes the vertex label x in {0,...,7} in binary (n = 8); second register, target of the modular shift and control for the marked coin.

specification.initial_state: |psi_0> = H^{\otimes 2}|00>_coin ⊗ H^{\otimes 3}|000>_pos, i.e. the uniform superposition of eq_2 over all 32 coin-position basis states.

steps.description: Prepare the uniform superposition over coin and position registers with Hadamards on all 5 qubits.

Repeat t times: apply the marked-dependent coin C (Grover coin on the coin register for x ≠ w, implemented by the Grover coin followed by a correction, or equivalently a position-controlled selection; -I on x = w realised by X^{⊗3} ... multi-controlled Z ... X^{⊗3} on the position register, no oracle), then apply the shift S as four coin-controlled modular ±1 and ±m adders on the position register.
Measure the position register in the computational basis and record the outcome x; the walk is successful if x = w.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of the 3-qubit position register (coin register discarded or traced out); outcome x in {0,...,7}. Success event: x = w = 0, with probability P_w(t) from eq_6.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Verify classically that the measured x is adjacent to the intended marked structure (here trivially x = w); if not, repeat the whole procedure. To choose t for the tiny instance, scan t over a small range (e.g. 0..10) and pick the t maximising P_w(t), since the abstract gives only the asymptotic O(sqrt(n)) scaling.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was provided, so a single tiny instance (n = 8 circulant graph with offsets ±1, ±3, one marked vertex w = 0) was chosen as the reconstruction target.
The paper's twisted toroid family is modelled by a degree-4 circulant graph; the true definition may differ.

Discrete-time coined walk with Grover coin on unmarked vertices and -I coin on the marked vertex (SKW-style) is assumed; the paper's actual coin and walk model (coined vs. Szegedy vs. continuous-time) is not stated in the abstract.
Register ordering coin ⊗ position with binary integer encoding of vertex labels; moving (coin-preserving) shift.
The decomposition of the stated O(sqrt(n) log n) gate count into O(sqrt(n)) steps of O(log n) gates each is an inference.

The number of walk steps t and the resulting success probabilities from the paper's numerical analysis.
